messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: service="inference-api-prod" symptom="pgbouncer max_clients reached" severity=P1 — connections rejected, high 5xx rate. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-7692 :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: Page sent to primary on-call @alex, escalation policy=eng-oncall-core. Auto-reminder in 2m.
alex: ack — looking
alex: seeing 500 spikes on /generate, logs show: 
```
2026-03-15T09:02:12Z ERROR db: could not get connection: no available connections (max_clients=200)
2026-03-15T09:02:13Z WARN pgbouncer: pool-size hit for db inference_main
```
alex: paging db on-call and pgbouncer owners. @mike can you confirm pgbouncer pods?
mike: on it, checking k8s and pgbouncer stats now
mike: pgbouncer pods (2/2) healthy but connections=~210 each, max_clients config = 200. clients_waiting climbing.
alex: looks like connection queueing, likely sudden traffic spike from hosted batch jobs. We need quick mitigation to reduce user impact.
natalie: CS note: multiple customers reporting failures for batch ingest and some high-rate inference tenants seeing 502s. Counting impacted orgs now — currently 8 active incidents from customers.
ops-bot: Alerting suggestion: temporarily enable reject_on_overflow and reduce per-tenant concurrency to 4 — runbook: DB-POOL-EXHAUST v2.
alex: ok plan: 1) scale pgbouncer to 4 replicas 2) enable request-rate limiter in API for anonymous/batch routes 3) temporarily toggle feature flag for large-batch mode -> queued. Will execute in that order.
mike: scaling pgbouncer now: 
```bash
kubectl -n infra scale deployment pgbouncer --replicas=4
```
mike: scaled, waiting for pods to warm. 
ops-bot: Reminder: increasing replicas increases pool capacity but may spike connections to Postgres, watch DB32 CPU/active connections.
alex: good point — hold on DB scaling until we see effect. Also enabling pgbouncer stats dump: 
```
echo "show pools" | psql postgres://admin@pgbouncer:6432/pgbouncer
```
sara: enabling rate limiter on /batch endpoints (threshold=10rps)
sara: toggled flag in prod: feature.batch_throttle = true — applying config.
mike: new pgbouncer pods ready, per-pod client_count now ~110, total headroom restored. client_waiting=0.
alex: checking error rate — 5xx down from 18% -> 3% over last 5m. Good. Keep monitoring.
natalie: update to CS: "We've applied mitigation to reduce connection pressure and are monitoring — some requests may be slower, but most customers are back to normal. We'll follow up with root cause and postmortem."
PagerDuty: Alert escalated to secondary on-call (sara) due to repeated reminders; notification sent.
alex: I'm going to hand off active monitoring to @sara in 10m and start investigating root cause (suspect runaway batch job from analytics pipeline).
sara: ack, taking over monitoring, will watch dashboards and keep PD updated.
alex: quick diagnostic: dumped active queries — many long-running INSERTs from job=analytics-bulk-child with age ~2-3m. Suspect runaway job.
mike: killed a few stuck client connections on pgbouncer to free slots: 
```
psql -c "SELECT * FROM pgbouncer.kill_cancel_waiting()"
```
(used our internal helper).
sara: metrics: pg_active_connections peaked at 950, now stable ~420. 5xx ~1.2% and trending down.
natalie: CS: started sending targeted messages to affected customers and opened a priority ticket for any who request SLA credit.
ops-bot: Note: auto-retry loops on client-side can worsen pool exhaustion. Recommend contacting top 3 offending tenants to implement backoff.
alex: opened an internal ticket ENG-1429 to throttle analytics-bulk jobs and add per-tenant concurrency caps. Adding owners: alex, mike, sara.
sara: PD note: I'll ack PD and mark as under investigation, will escalate to DB infra if we see another spike.
PagerDuty: Alert acknowledged by sara.
alex: follow-ups before handoff: 1) confirm no scheduled batch jobs in the last deploy window 2) check for sudden traffic from any API key 3) smoke test: run small batch to verify behavior.
mike: verified no scheduled deploy, traffic spike correlates with analytics pipeline job started at 08:59 UTC. Identified offending job instance id=analytics-7823.
sara: running smoke test: small single request to /generate -> success, latency 120ms.
alex: ok handing off: @sara you take post-incident watch for next 2 hours; I'll dig deeper into root cause and CL on ENG-1429.
sara: taking handoff — will keep PD updated and loop in DB infra if connections >700 again.
natalie: will prepare customer post-incident note and share draft in #customer-impact later today.
ops-bot: Closing note: mitigation successful, but recommended follow-ups: permanent pgbouncer config tweak, per-tenant concurrency enforcement, and alert tuning to reduce PD loops.
PagerDuty: Incident resolved? Pending manual resolve by on-call.
sara: marking PD incident as resolved — moving to postmortem.
PagerDuty: Incident INC-7692 resolved by sara.
alex: thanks team. Adding timeline and notes to ENG-1429 and will schedule a blameless postmortem tomorrow.
sara: handing active monitoring to next shift @mike at 11:00 UTC — leaving notes in the runbook. :white_check_mark:
